## 1. What this application is

`u2giants/shared-db` is the canonical repository for **one** Supabase PostgreSQL database shared by five separate applications, each living in its own repo:

| App | Status | Repo |
|---|---|---|
| PopDAM (digital asset management) | live | `u2giants/popdam3` |
| PopCRM | live | `u2giants/popcrm-web` |
| DesignFlow PLM ("dflow") | live | `popcre/designflow-*` (six repos) |
| PopPIM (product information) | in development | `u2giants/poppim-web` |
| monitor | live | `u2giants/synology-monitor` |

Every schema/DDL change is authored **here**, proved on the **preview** database (`rjyboqwcdzcocqgmsyel`), then promoted to **production** (`qsllyeztdwjgirsysgai`). There is no "just my app" change — one bad migration breaks all five, and it is usually found days later by a user rather than by a test.

**Who works here:** AI sessions (Claude, Codex, GLM, Grok, Kimi, Qwen), frequently **3–7 at once**, across several machines, sometimes **in the same working copy**. The owner, **Albert Hazan**, is a business owner and **explicitly not a programmer** — AI sessions are the entire engineering department. **Controls must be mechanical; anything that depends on a human remembering a written rule will not happen.** That single fact drove every decision below.

**Branch model:** branch + PR, and **the AI merges its own PRs**. (This is specific to `shared-db`. Do *not* self-merge in the dflow repos.)

**Stack relevant to this work:** plain Node.js ESM scripts under `scripts/`, no build step, no framework. Tests are `node --test`.

## 2. What we set out to do this session, and why

**In business terms:** stop two AI agents being sent to change the same part of the database at the same time — *before* either does the work, so nobody's work is thrown away.

It began as something much smaller. Albert asked me to clean up a handoff folder he believed was at a file cap. It wasn't. Investigating led to the real problem, and he then asked the question that redirected the whole session:

> *"do we have rules that are gumming up the process and should maybe be changed?"*

and then, decisively:

> *"i don't want collision prevention to happen at the merge gate, it has to be prevented before all the work is done. the orchestrator has to know not to hand out work that would collide BEFORE IT HANDS OUT THE WORK."*

That is the actual objective. He is right, and it is the standard the design is now held to.

### The incidents that make this real (all documented in-repo, all verified)

1. **2026-07-31 — the four-way collision.** Four independent sessions each authored a migration doing `create or replace function plm.promote_coldlion_source_owned`. That statement is last-writer-wins, so merging any two would have **silently erased** the other. **All four passed CI.** Documented in the header of `.github/workflows/pr-object-collision.yml`.
2. **Duplicate migration timestamps, twice** (`20260722220000`, `20260728160000`). Supabase keys its migration ledger on the 14-digit version **alone**, so one migration was **silently skipped** while the ledger reported success (`AGENTS.md` rule 5).
3. **A 442-row production `DELETE`** from `ingest.raw_record` by a session that believed it was connected to preview (`AGENTS.md` §4.2, line ~622).
4. **Nine PRs (#442–#450) merged entirely outside coordinator control**, and **two coordinator sessions active four minutes apart** on 2026-08-06.

### The process finding underneath it

Measured, not impressionistic: **~12,700 lines of rules/process docs**; the coordinator queue grew **0 → 68 items in six days and never once shrank**; two *required* CI checks were themselves defective; and two mandatory rules **deadlocked** (a retention rule requires archiving blocks that a CI check requires stay). `AGENTS.md` itself says the discipline is *"a MANUAL discipline, not automation."*

## 4. Everything we tried that did NOT work

**Read this section before designing anything.** Four models argued this out and several confident answers were wrong — including mine. Each of these cost real time; none should be re-derived.

1. **`git push` as an atomic claim lock — MY idea, and it is broken.** I proposed `git push origin HEAD:refs/db-claims/<version>`, reasoning that a ref push is server-arbitrated. **Tested live: a *descendant* commit fast-forwards straight over an existing ref and silently steals the lock.** A non-descendant is rejected, which is what fooled me on the first test. **Never use a plain `git push` as a create-only primitive.** The correct primitive is `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/git/refs`, which returns `422 Reference already exists` and has no fast-forward path. Both behaviours verified.

2. **"GitHub refuses custom ref namespaces like `refs/db-claims/*`" — GLM 5.2 asserted this; it is FALSE.** Tested: the push was accepted, and so was the REST create. Do not "fix" the namespace on GLM's advice.

3. **A database registry table (`app.migration_claim`) with `version text primary key`** — GLM 5.2's recommendation, described as *"the only concurrency-safe option."* **Rejected, and GLM withdrew it when challenged.** It puts database credentials on the **dispatch path** — the hot path every task crosses — to solve a *wasted-work* problem, in a repo that already had a 442-row production `DELETE` from a session that thought it was on preview. Blast-radius asymmetry kills it. **Do not reintroduce without Albert's sign-off.**

4. **A two-phase transaction (ref + issue) with rollback, ownership metadata and a reconciliation command** — Codex required this before shipping version reservation. **I argued it was over-engineered and Codex withdrew it.** An orphaned *version* ref wastes one integer from an unbounded space and is invisible in the branch list. Codex then improved on my position: **keep version refs permanently**, because the preview ledger is persistent and holds every version ever pushed, so releasing a number for reuse could collide with one preview already recorded. ⚠️ **This does NOT apply to object refs** — see §5.

5. **Fixing only the printed message ("remove the word SAFE")** — my first plan draft. Codex showed it is **partly cosmetic**: the field is literally named `safe` (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:177`) and the usage text defines exit 0 as "safe to dispatch" (`:400`). Grepping for "SAFE" stops working; `if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)` does not. Renaming a string does not change what a script does.

6. **"Broaden `PATTERNS`" as a single flat list shared by both checks** — my second draft. Codex showed it conflates **one parser** (right) with **one collision policy** (wrong). The merge guard is a *required* check built around whole-object replacement and its failure messages say so; making it report every table touched would make its own explanations false and risks alarm fatigue. Correct shape: the parser returns structured operations `{action, kind, target}` and each consumer applies its own policy.

7. **Check first, then claim in a separate step** — the shape of the merged tool. Grok 4.5 identified this as the central defect: it is a time-of-check/time-of-use race, and the 2026-07-31 incident is *exactly* the case where both agents pass the check before either claims. In its words, **"a race reporter with extra steps, not a lock."**

8. **Claims as GitHub-issue bodies parsed with a mini-language** — the merged design. An issue body is **not** create-if-absent, so it cannot serialise anything. It also needed a hand-rolled parser that produced **four reproduced defects in a single day** — worst of which: *a single `#` comment line silently drops every object*, turning a claim into an empty claim that can never collide.

9. **The claim command as a bash heredoc** — Grok's catch, and an uncomfortable one. `claimCommand` emits `--body "$(cat <<'CLAIM' … )"`, and **this machine is PowerShell-first.** So "zero claims have ever been filed" was **partly a tooling failure, not only a discipline failure** — the prescribed path did not work on the host it was prescribed for. Any printed command must use `gh issue create --body-file <path>` or `gh api` with a JSON body.

10. **Applying the Part B2.2 retention rule during the queue sweep (PR #463).** Attempted, then deliberately abandoned: the three oldest `COMPLETED` blocks are `B8`/`B13`/`B14`, which the required `Backlog / queue sync` check matches **only via a prose mention**. Archiving them would break that check the moment it is repaired. **Fix the guard first, then archive.** The reasoning is written into `COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` so it is not re-derived.

11. **`gh run rerun --failed` to clear stranded CI runs — insufficient.** See §5; this cost about two hours of wall-clock.

12. **Closing and reopening the PR to force fresh CI runs — does not work.** The stranded runs hold the commit SHA. Only a new SHA schedules new runs.

## 5. Root causes and key findings

**A. The parser blind spot is the root cause of the false-safe.** `extractObjects` (`check-pr-object-collisions.mjs:235`) iterates a fixed `PATTERNS` list (`:128`) of six object kinds in `create`/`drop` forms only — **no `alter` verb of any kind**. Acceptable for a merge-time backstop (its header admits it at `:62`), not acceptable for a tool that prints a verdict.

**B. The 23 existing tests cannot catch it, and this is the most important finding for whoever writes the fix.** The helper at `check-dispatch-collision.test.mjs:73`:

```js
const CLAIM = (label, objects, version = null) => ({ label, objects, version, url: `https://x/${label}` })
```

injects object arrays **directly**. No test routes real SQL through `extractObjects` into `findDispatchConflicts`. **If `extractObjects` returned `[]` for every input, the entire suite would still pass.** Step 2 of the plan writes that missing test.

**C. The lock was on the wrong thing.** Version reservation was made atomic; object claiming was not. But the incident was same-*object*, and duplicate versions are **already blocked at merge** by `scripts/check-sql.sh`. Hence the redesign: **acquisition IS the check.** Verified live 2026-08-06 — object-encoding ref names are legal, the second `POST` returns 422, and every holder is listable in one call:

```bash
gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/git/matching-refs/db-claims/objects --jq '.[]|"\(.ref) -> \(.object.sha[0:7])"'
```

**D. ⚠️ TWO REF LIFETIMES THAT MUST NEVER BE CONFUSED.** They sit side by side in the plan and look contradictory:

- **Version refs → kept permanently** (plan D13). An integer from an unbounded space; the preview ledger is persistent, so reuse is dangerous.
- **Object refs → always released** (plan D16). Never releasing one **freezes that object forever.**

Confusing these would lock the schema. Partial acquisition therefore needs rollback for *object* refs even though rollback was rejected for *version* refs — different lifetimes, different rules.

**E. `AGENTS.md` §6.7 was stale and it actively misled a reviewer.** The table claimed `strict: false` and four required contexts; live was `strict: true` and six. **Grok read the stale table and reported the (correct) plan as carrying wrong facts.** Fixed in PR #467. The generalisable lesson, which Kimi named: documents may hold **decisions and reasoning** (which do not decay), but **anything queryable must carry the command, not the answer.**

**F. The stranded-CI-run trap.** During a GitHub Actions `major_outage`, two required checks were left at `status=queued, conclusion=null, attempt=1`, not updating for hours. GitHub **refused to cancel them** (`Cannot cancel a workflow run that is completed`) **while still reporting them as queued**. They can never report, so the PR stays `BLOCKED` forever. `gh run rerun` and close/reopen both fail. **Only an empty commit (moving the SHA) frees it.** Now recorded as plan §11.12.

**G. ⚠️ THE SHARED-CHECKOUT HAZARD — this bit hard and will bite you.** `C:\repos\shared-db` is shared with other live sessions. Another session committed its OPA work at the moment this session created a branch, so **the branch silently inherited that session's commit `48680a3`.** That work later reached `main` by a different route **including commit `4f99ccf`, which retracts the claim `48680a3` made.** Merging `main` then conflicted in **three files this session never touched**, and the branch was carrying a retracted claim toward `main`. Resolved by taking `origin/main`'s version for all three. Now recorded as plan §11.13.

### Phase A — urgent (start here)

1. **Step 1 — remove the verdict, in all four places.** Delete `SAFE TO DISPATCH` (`check-dispatch-collision.mjs:206`); rename `result.safe` → `overlapFound` (`:177`) through `findDispatchConflicts`, `formatReport` and `--json`; reword the exit-code docs (`:400`); derive the "checked classes" list from `PATTERNS` rather than hard-coding it.
   *You'll know it worked when:* `node scripts/check-dispatch-collision.mjs --task t --objects "function plm.foo" | grep -i safe` returns nothing, and `node --test scripts/check-dispatch-collision.test.mjs` passes.

2. **Step 1b — disable `--allocate-version`** (`:444`). Make it exit 2 with an explanation; correct the false comment on `nextFreeVersion` (`:190`) that claims it "kills the duplicate-timestamp class."
   *You'll know it worked when:* the flag prints the explanation and `echo $?` shows `2`.

3. **Step 2 — write the failing DDL tests.** Route real `alter table` / `create table` / `create index` / `grant` SQL through `extractObjects` into `findDispatchConflicts`.
   ⚠️ **Run them red LOCALLY and paste the output into the PR body — do NOT open a PR whose tip is red.** That suite runs inside the *required* `Cross-PR object collision` job, so a red tip can never merge.
   *You'll know it worked when:* they fail before step 3 and pass after.

4. **Step 2b — fix the five gatherer defects** in `gatherOpenPrObjects` (`:322–349`): draft PRs are excluded (`:326`, wrong for dispatch); only the first migration's version is captured (`:334`); deleted files are fetched anyway; the filename is unencoded (`:335` — use `encodeURIComponent` **per segment**, *not* `encodeURI`, which does not encode `#`); the base64 Contents fetch can silently truncate where the sibling uses raw.
   *You'll know it worked when:* one unit test per defect passes.

Steps 3a (historical noise gate), 3b (structured operations), 4 (`--sql` primary), **5 (`--claim`: atomic object refs — the core change)**, 5b (release on merge + staleness).

## 7. Constraints and gotchas in force

1. **Branch + PR; you merge it yourself.** Never commit to `main` directly.
2. **Commit identity must be `Albert Hazan <u2giants@users.noreply.github.com>`.** Check `git var GIT_COMMITTER_IDENT` **before** your first commit — 231 wrong-identity commits already reached shared branches and cannot be fixed.
3. **No database contact is needed for any step in this plan.** No migration, no preview/production push, no `supabase` CLI, no Supabase MCP, no `psql`.
4. **Branch protection: `strict: true`, six required checks, `enforce_admins: true`.** Your branch must be up to date before merging.
5. **Never weaken `check-pr-object-collisions.mjs`'s `Skip`-to-green posture** — a *required* gate that cannot gather inputs must warn and pass, or it blocks every PR. The dispatch tool's opposite posture (unknown ⇒ exit 2) is also deliberate. **Do not "harmonise" them.**
6. **Never rename the CI job `Cross-PR object collision`** — it is a required status context; renaming it makes every future PR hang forever.
7. **No band-aids, no silent failures.** Every fallback must be loud.
8. **`shared-db` is a PUBLIC repo.** Do not create issues, labels, or other public content without asking Albert.
9. **Clean up every test ref you create.** Verify with `gh api repos/u2giants/shared-db/git/matching-refs/db-claims --jq '.[].ref'` returning empty.
10. **⚠️ You may be sharing this checkout with another live session** — see §5G. Before opening a PR run `git diff origin/main --stat` and confirm it lists **only** files you meant to change. Never `git add -A`; stage explicit paths. **Uncommitted changes you did not make are another session's live work — leave them.**
11. **Do not delete `.ai/deepseek-sessions/` or `.ai/reviews/`** (untracked, not yours).
12. **Windows line endings:** `.mjs` edits show a `LF will be replaced by CRLF` warning. Harmless; do not "fix" it and do not reformat whole files.
13. **`COORDINATOR_INTAKE.md` blocks are moved only by the coordinator**, and only forward.

## Self-audit (mandatory gate — completed before this handoff was shown)

**1. Could a brand-new developer with no project knowledge pick up where I left off and not skip a beat?** Yes. §1 defines the five dependent apps, the branch model, the databases and who works here; §3 gives every merged SHA and states plainly which artefact is currently wrong and why it is not an active fire; §6 gives numbered steps with `file:line` targets and a verification gate each; §7 and §8 cover the traps and the environment. *Gap found during audit and fixed:* the first draft did not say that **nobody is currently relying on the broken tool** — without that a newcomer could reasonably treat it as a production incident and panic-revert. Added to §3.

**2. Could they continue as effectively as I can right now?** Yes. §4 records **twelve** dead ends, including three where I was wrong (the `git push` lock, "remove the word SAFE is enough", the flat `PATTERNS` list) and two where a reviewer was wrong (GLM on ref namespaces, Codex on the transaction). §5 records the seven findings that each cost real time, with the exact commands that settled them. *Gap found and fixed:* the first draft omitted that the 23 tests would pass even if `extractObjects` returned `[]` for everything — that is the single most important fact for whoever writes step 2, now called out as finding **B**.

**3. Is every detail needed for flawless execution included?** Yes — background (§1–2), current state with SHAs (§3), failures (§4), findings (§5), exact next actions with gates (§6), constraints (§7), access (§8), risks and dated decisions (§9). Secrets are referenced by vault and item only. *Gap found and fixed:* the two ref **lifetimes** were described only in the plan; because confusing them would freeze the schema, they are now also stated here as finding **D**.

**Checklist:** all 9 sections present; part (b) explicitly N/A with reason; a newcomer could proceed without asking a question; dead ends included with why they failed; every step has a verification gate; every SHA, path and identifier defined; commit/push/merge status explicit for each PR; no secret values. **All items pass.**
